title: Asthma treatment, age 12+ (BTS/NICE/SIGN 2024)
steps: Check FeNO/eosinophils: refer if raised, otherwise add LTRA or LAMA

Increase the regular ICS dose before adding anything else.

title: Asthma diagnosis in adults

title: Acute severe asthma
whys: Correct hypoxia first, aiming for 93–95%.
Salbutamol relieves bronchospasm fastest; repeat or give back-to-back.

Magnesium relaxes bronchial smooth muscle if there's a poor response.
If still deteriorating, ICU may use aminophylline or ventilation.

title: COPD inhalers (NICE)
whys: Short-acting bronchodilators relieve breathlessness when needed.

title: Hypertension (NICE NG136)
steps: ACEi/ARB (<55 or T2DM) or CCB (≥55 or Black)
Add the other of ACEi/ARB and CCB, or a thiazide-like diuretic
Spironolactone if K⁺ ≤4.5, otherwise α- or β-blocker
whys: Younger and diabetic patients respond to RAAS blockade; over 55 or Black patients respond better to CCBs.
Add the other first-line class, or a thiazide-like diuretic.

At step 4, spironolactone works well if potassium allows; otherwise an alpha- or beta-blocker.

title: Type 2 diabetes drugs (NICE NG28)
steps: Metformin (add SGLT2i if CVD, HF or high CV risk)
Add a second drug (DPP-4i, pioglitazone, sulfonylurea or SGLT2i)
Triple therapy, or GLP-1 RA if BMI ≥35
whys: Diet, weight loss and education come first and underpin everything else.
Metformin is first line; add an SGLT2 inhibitor early if there's cardiovascular or heart failure risk.
If HbA1c is still above target, add a second agent chosen for the patient.
Triple therapy, or a GLP-1 agonist if obese, comes next.
Insulin when other options fail or glucose is very high.

title: Heart failure with reduced EF
steps: Specialist: switch to sacubitril/valsartan, ivabradine, CRT/ICD

Add a rate-limiting calcium channel blocker

title: Stable angina
steps: GTN as needed + aspirin and statin
Add long-acting nitrate, ivabradine, nicorandil or ranolazine
